problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with normal vector $\overset{~}{n},$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,y,\,x⟩\,,\,\overset{~}{n}(x,y,z)=⟨2y,\,-z,\,2x⟩\,,\,n=\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}\frac{\boxed{}}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S
$$

what is the missing expression?
worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector $\overset{~}{n}.$ By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨2y,\,-z,\,2x⟩}{\sqrt{(2y)^{2}+(-z)^{2}+(2x)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨2y,\,-z,\,2x⟩}{\sqrt{4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+4{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨2y,\,-z,\,2x⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨z,\,y,\,x⟩\cdot \frac{⟨2y,\,-z,\,2x⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨z,\,y,\,x⟩\cdot ⟨2y,\,-z,\,2x⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2yz-yz+2{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+yz}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\,\frac{2{x}^{2}+yz}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S.\end{aligned}
$$
